newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds futures flirt with 12-week highs.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds futures flirt with 12-week highs.

text.p: Australian bond futures continued the recovery from their post-budget sell-off, striking 12-week highs around mid-morning after further stops were triggered off.

Traders said there was a general feeling that the market had overdone the sell-off on its disappointment over the budget outcome earlier in the week, and a continuation of a rebound in U.S. Treasuries during Tokyo trade was fuelling the move.

However, some traders were surprised by the move in the short end, particularly in the bill strip, given the Reserve Bank's concern over wages growth, reiterated by its governor Ian Macfarlane on Thursday.

"Sure (Macfarlane) mentioned the easing word twice, but he also said the tightening word once which seems to have gone completely over the market's head. I can't see any reason to be buying at these levels," said one bemused trader.

Macfarlane also said that the central bank would let the economy grow faster as long as there was no threat to inflation suggesting that official interest rates could be on hold at 6.0 percent for sometime to come.
However, despite the firm tone of the bill strip, the March 1998 contract is still factoring in a 50 basis point hike, while near June and September are only a shade below 6.0 percent.

Local debt continued to show an outperforming bias against the U.S., although spreads were slightly above their initial lows. The U.S. weakened on a jump in core April CPI and a drop in jobless claims on Thursday, but rebounded on flat industrial production and a fall in capacity utilisation.
